Serious

Analytics running with no privacy policy posted

CalOPPAState privacy lawssite-wide

Your site runs Google Analytics and has a contact form, so it collects visitor data, but there is no privacy policy link anywhere on the page. CalOPPA and the newer state privacy laws expect any site that collects personal information to post one. This is usually a quick add, and it is the kind of gap that privacy complaints point at first.

Images with no alt text

WCAG 1.1.15 images

Five images on the page have no alt text, so a screen reader skips them and a blind visitor gets nothing about what they show. On a marketing site that is your brand and portfolio imagery going unread, and it is the most common thing ADA accessibility complaints cite.

Moderate

Heading levels are out of order

WCAG 1.3.14 places

The page's headings skip levels in four spots. Screen-reader users navigate by heading structure, and a broken outline makes the page harder to move through. It also muddies how search engines read the page, which matters for a marketing site.

Scope & method

This is an automated scan of your homepage. Accessibility is checked with axe-core, the open-source engine from Deque Systems that most teams treat as the industry standard, against WCAG 2.1 Levels A and AA. Privacy is a check for tracking scripts and whether a privacy policy is posted.

A full picture needs every page reviewed plus manual testing, and these are technical exposure signals, not a legal determination. Whether a given law applies depends on your size and where your visitors are, which is a question for your counsel. We are flagging what the tools see so nothing sits unnoticed.
